guidance_summary: Q3 2026 revenue guided to approximately $13.0 billion, plus or minus $300 million, implying 41% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to remain approximately 56%, with operating expenses of about $3.65 billion; management gave no specific capex guidance. Management expects server CPU revenue to grow more than 80% year over year in the second half of 2026, more than 70% in 2027, and total data center revenue to more than double year over year in 2027, while substantially exceeding its prior long-term targets of 35% revenue growth and $20 annual EPS.
key_qa_moments: Analysts questioned whether data center growth and the implied 2027 GPU revenue trajectory were being understated. Su repeatedly emphasized that data center AI growth would be well above 100% in 2027, said the cited GPU revenue framework was too low, and characterized OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic demand as very strong.

Analysts pressed on Helios gross margins during the initial ramp. Hu acknowledged that data center AI margins are slightly below the company average and avoided giving a quarterly margin profile, citing mix, improving yields, server CPU growth, and embedded recovery as offsets.

On supply constraints, Su gave unusually direct detail: server CPU supply is currently tight because demand was unforecasted, but 2027 supply should improve. She cited wafers, back-end capacity, packaging, substrates, and other components as potential constraints, while saying AMD has enough visibility to support the stated growth.

When asked about revenue per gigawatt and 2027 capacity, Su provided only a broad double-digit-billion-dollar monetization range and said AMD has supply to more than meet current guidance, with upside dependent on customer data-center build timing and additional capacity.
risks: Server CPU and Helios ramps are dependent on tight supply chains spanning advanced-node wafers, packaging, substrates, HBM, and other system components.
Initial Helios products are highly complex and early yields are expected to improve over the next several quarters, creating execution and margin risk during ramp.
Data center AI margins are currently slightly below AMD's corporate average, and 2027 gross margin will depend heavily on the mix between accelerator and higher-margin CPU revenue.
Customer data-center readiness, power availability, and build-out timing could delay or change the cadence of the large 2027 deployments.
Management expects a softer PC market in the second half of 2026 as memory and component costs rise, while gaming remains pressured by the console cycle and higher component costs.
The very large 2027 outlook relies on successful execution with a limited group of strategic AI customers and continued ROCm ecosystem adoption.
summary: AMD reported a highly bullish quarter, with 50% revenue growth, 56% gross margin, data center revenue above half of company sales, and major upward revisions to its long-term opportunity and earnings trajectory. The Q&A reinforced strong CPU demand and substantial Helios upside, although management was less specific on accelerator revenue cadence and margins and acknowledged supply, yield, customer build-out, and memory-cost risks.
